slot.brief: Show an asymmetric ether (figure) treated with excess HI; identify both products and note why the cleavage occurs at the bond giving the stable carbocation/SN1 path.

stem: The ether shown is treated with excess HI. Which pair of organic products forms, and what accounts for the cleavage?
options: 2-Iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane; cleavage proceeds via the stable tertiary carbocation
1-Iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane; cleavage proceeds via a primary carbocation
2-Iodo-2-methylpropane and ethanol; the alcohol is not further cleaved by excess HI
1-Iodopropane and iodomethane; cleavage occurs at both sides of the oxygen

verdicts.working: The ether is ethyl tert-butyl ether. HI cleaves the C–O bond on the tertiary side via a stable tertiary carbocation; excess HI converts the resulting ethanol to iodoethane. The products are 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane.

working:
$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-O-CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI}$ cleaves at the tertiary side via $\text{S}_\text{N}1$.\
$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ form initially.\
Excess HI converts ethanol to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{I}$; final organic products: tert-butyl iodide and iodoethane.

Independent check: The ether is ethyl tert-butyl ether. HI cleaves the C–O bond on the tertiary side via a stable tertiary carbocation; excess HI converts the resulting ethanol to iodoethane. The products are 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane.
solution:
Protonation of the ether is followed by C–O cleavage at the tertiary side via the stable tert-butyl carbocation:
$$ (CH_3)_3C-O-CH_2CH_3 \xrightarrow{HI} (CH_3)_3C-I + CH_3CH_2OH $$
Excess HI converts ethanol to iodoethane, giving 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and iodoethane.
